currentContext.business: Cinevista is engaged in the business of Content Production for Television, Films and Digital Platforms, supplying programming to satellite channels; the Directors' Report states there has been no change in the business of the Company during FY 2025-26. Alongside content, the company has, in the words of management, moved on from being just a media outlet to becoming developers too, having changed the end use of its studio parcel of land and entered a joint development agreement with KRCREPL, registered on 29 May 2023, under which the Residential-Cum-Retail project 'Antares' commenced in late November 2024 at the junction of JVLR and LBS Marg. A third strand is a set of owned YouTube channels on the Google platform spanning general entertainment, youth, music and regional-language programming.

currentContext.expansion: Cinevista's expansion is not manufacturing capacity but a real-estate development on its own studio land. Management changed the end use of the studio parcel of land after the pandemic and, after roughly three years of searching for a partner, inked a joint development project with KRCREPL, registering the joint development agreement on 29 May 2023. Post approvals, the Residential-Cum-Retail project 'Antares' commenced in late November 2024 at the junction of JVLR and LBS Marg, Mumbai, and is registered under MahaRERA Registration No. P51800077483; work started on the project in November 2024, 17 months after the JDA was registered. The project will see its completion only by November 2029, which management calls a good 3.5 years ahead, and it describes the partner as the 7th largest developer in the country. Against this, at the end of FY 2025-2026 the company had received a total of Rs 35.37 Crores as its share of revenue to date, including sums received in FY 2024-2025. Management adds that the company will continue to make strategic investments in land and building, and in projects where it sees potential for growth and profitability. The second, asset-light expansion track is digital: six YouTube channels on the Google platform (Cinevista Classics, Swift & Fast, Cinevista Entertainment, the recently added music channel Gyan Sagar, Cinevista Marathi and Cinevista Gujarati), with a Kannada channel and a Malayalam channel to be launched in the near future.
currentContext.mdna: The KRC joint development project is the central value driver; the company has received a total of Rs 35.37 crores as its share of revenue to date (including sums received in FY 2024-25), with the project completing only by November 2029|Management frames the next three to four years as of great significance and importance, and expects to push for progress and growth over that window|YouTube is described as a slow-growing business that, once established, is a winner all the way; scale is being built through subscribers, views and watch time across six channels|Regional-language and music channels (Cinevista Marathi, Cinevista Gujarati, Gyan Sagar, plus planned Kannada and Malayalam) are the stated route to widening the digital audience base|Core business unchanged: the Directors' Report states the Company remains engaged in Content Production for Television, Films and Digital Platforms with no change in business during FY 2025-26|No order book or contracted pipeline is quantified. Management states only that 'There are some things in the pipeline, which we're working on, with intense fervour & zest', to be shared with shareholders on an immediate basis once there is total clarity.

risks.risk: Qualified audit opinion on the FY26 standalone financial statements
risks.note: The auditor's opinion is expressly qualified: it gives a true and fair view 'except for the effects of the matter described in the Basis for Qualified Opinion paragraph'. A recurring qualification limits the reliability of the reported position and is a governance-level flag in its own right.

risks.risk: Carrying value of investments and advances in subsidiaries and associates
risks.note: The Basis for Qualified Opinion draws attention to Note 31 on management's assessment of the realisation of the carrying value of investments and advances in subsidiary and associate companies. If those balances are not realisable, the standalone balance sheet carries an overstated asset.

risks.risk: Substantial erosion in the net worth of subsidiary and associate companies
risks.note: The auditor records that the subsidiaries and associates in which the Company holds investments and advances have suffered substantial erosion in net worth, which puts the value of the group's non-core entities, and the recoverability of amounts advanced to them, in question.

risks.risk: Single-project dependence on the KRC joint development agreement
risks.note: The value narrative rests almost entirely on one project on one land parcel: the joint development agreement with KRCREPL registered on 29 May 2023, from which the Company has received Rs 35.37 crores of revenue share to date. There is no second development to absorb a setback.

risks.risk: Long completion runway and execution risk on 'Antares'
risks.note: Work started only in November 2024, 17 months after the JDA was registered, and the project 'will see its completion only by November 2029'. Management itself says this is a time when senior management needs to be on top of everything before the project reaches its finishing line, leaving roughly 3.5 years of construction, market and counterparty exposure.

risks.risk: Dependence on a single development partner
risks.note: The whole real-estate monetisation is with one counterparty, described as the 7th largest developer in the country. Management's own account of the search records the frustration of being let down many a time before the partner was found, showing how exposed the plan is to partner performance.

risks.risk: Regulatory and approvals dependence for the development project
risks.note: The project commenced only 'post approvals' and is registered under MahaRERA Registration No. P51800077483; continued regulatory compliance and approvals sit on the critical path of the revenue share.

risks.risk: Slow, unproven ramp of the digital / YouTube business as a diversification hedge
risks.note: The intended new revenue engine is acknowledged by management as 'a slow growing business' entered late, and further initiatives are only 'things in the pipeline' with no clarity yet, so it cannot be relied on to offset lumpiness in content production or in the development project.
